test_title: PYST 4: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 6 days. B alone can do the same work in 9 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete the work in 6 days.

B alone can complete the work in 9 days.

We need to find how long A alone will take to complete double the work.

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of A and B's individual work time.

Efficiency = Total work ÷ Time taken.

Time taken = Total work ÷ Efficiency.

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM(6, 9) = 18 units

Efficiency of A and B together = Total work ÷ Time taken = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of B alone = Total work ÷ Time taken = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 units/day

Efficiency of A alone = Efficiency of A and B together - Efficiency of B = 3 - 2 = 1 unit/day

Time taken by A alone to complete double the work = Total work × 2 ÷ Efficiency of A = 18 × 2 ÷ 1 = 36 days

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
